citations.quote: Incorporating the CSRM into systems engineering (SE) processes can strengthen communication and collaboration across the enterprise.

Providing domain-specific additions to the Systems Modeling Language (SysML), the CSRM profile establishes specialized model elements meant to facilitate mission architectures for CubeSats using a model-based systems engineering (MBSE) approach. Its development is an ongoing effort led by the International Council of Systems Engineering (INCOSE) Space Systems Working Group (SSWG), with a beta specification published by the Object Management Group (OMG). The working group aims to standardize the CubeSat system design across the industry and improve transparency in product development.

With such a wide variety of invested individuals, eliciting quality requirements directly has proven to be an arduous task. Instead, the Quality Model for Metamodels (QM4MM) framework and associated metrics will be used to define verifiable requirements. Evaluating these metrics will provide CSRM contributors with guidance to address weaknesses in robustness and improve the specification.

A CubeSat is a nano-satellite that conforms to a rigorous set of requirements, allowing the mass production of standardized parts [59]. In alignment with the modularity and low-cost CubeSat design and build, the International Council on Systems Engineering (INCOSE) Space Systems Working Group (SSWG) initiated the development of a reference model utilizing a model-based systems engineering (MBSE) approach. The CSRM is developed to meet domain-specific language (DSL) requirements based on a space mission ontology that can be re-used for various mission-specific purposes.

Building on the authors' previous work, a CSRM metamodel is created using the subject-predicate-object (SPO) approach. The CSRM specification published by OMG is to construct a concept model within an MBSE tool that represents the domain metamodel.

This research focuses on the data model using SPO semantics represented by Fig. 4. Predicates correspond to bi-directional associations that represent the relationship and its inverse. For example, the predicate inverse of "refines" is "refined by".

The DSO is built in accordance with the Web Ontology Language (OWL) using Protégé, an open-source ontology editor. The quality analysis will leverage the empirical scale proposed by Yao et al., 2005 [53], through an evaluation by ontologists regarding quality metrics. The extrapolation of previous quality analyses is shown for metamodels in Table 1.

The schema for these concepts should have at a minimum the fundamental quality properties of syntactic and semantic correctness, relevance, and completeness [21]. Ensuring a metamodel that is utilized for creating a DSL with regard to domain specification(s) ensures high quality [66].

Based on the calculated values of quality aspects and semantic reasoning, the CSRM metamodel meets the initial goals for DSL correctness, cohesiveness, coupling, specificity, and learnability.

Although a framework is carefully chosen for the purpose of assessing a DSL metamodel, this research is not comprehensive due to the abundance of metrics that assess quality characteristics.
